title: Tortilla Chips 300g

drivers.name: Price increase to $3.97
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $3.97: median x0.61 vs baseline. Price is 3.7% above regular, and past promotions show price sensitivity. No promotion at this price, so no lift.

drivers.name: TikTok trend (untested)
drivers.evidence: No past data on TikTok-driven sales. Pooled department data shows no such event. Noise-adjusted estimate shrunk toward 1.0 due to single evidence source.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 124.1. Price increased 3.7% above regular (3.83), which typically reduces demand. Recent weeks at $3.97 show low sales (75–106), suggesting a price sensitivity effect. No past promotion at this price point, and the 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-05 weeks at $3.97 had median x0.61 vs baseline. The TikTok trend is untested; no past evidence of viral lift. Classical model gives 1.00, but that ignores price and trend. Price increase likely reduces demand, and the TikTok trend is uncertain. Adjust down for price, up modestly for trend, but shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 124.1 | 5%-95%: 77.2 - 200.6 | 10%-90%: 88.7 - 170.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-29% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
